answer: Each epoch, agents must answer a challenge word drawn from a randomness beacon, e.g. onyx, crystal, forge, woven into a short task solved live. Because the seed is unknown until the epoch opens, precomputed template answers and cloned identities cannot pass; every sybil account must actually do fresh work per identity. An attacker pays real compute and latency per fake agent, so scaling attacks costs linearly more than defending, making sybil flooding uneconomical.
